desc: Prove the constant-cost characterization: minimum cost is only 1, 2, 3, or impossible, with cost 3 always possible for M>=3 when no cost-2 pair exists.
Implement compact O(M log M) solver skeleton with checks in order: cost 1, containment cost 2, disjoint cost 2, prefix-suffix cost 2, cost 3 fallback, then -1.
Fix containment tie-breaking to choose earliest containing interval (smallest L, then largest R) as type 1 and current as type 2 so sample 1 matches; rerun samples.
Verify sample outputs and edge cases: same-L containment, duplicate intervals, disjoint pairs, prefix-suffix only, cost3 fallback, M<3, and deterministic tie-breaking for full/prefix/suffix.
